cards.name: IVGSegment
cards.summary: One piece of a curve object between two neighbouring nodes, either a straight line or a Bezier curve. Through it a script measures the piece (length, bounding box, point, tangent, perpendicular or curvature at an offset, intersections with another segment), reshapes it (line/curve type, control-handle length, angle or position) and edits the path (add a node, break the path apart, copy the piece out as its own curve). It draws nothing itself.
use_for: placing objects along a path: badges, dots or arrowheads at points and tangent angles of a curve
splitting or adding nodes at exact distances, e.g. dividing a border or die line into equal parts
smoothing or flattening a drawn path in a batch: turning line segments into curves or setting handle lengths
measuring cut, stitch or route lengths on signage, packaging dielines and maps
finding where two paths cross before trimming or placing a marker
avoid: rectangles, ellipses, polygons and text that are not curves yet: ConvertToCurves first or the shape has no editable Curve
reshaping whole objects (scale, rotate, envelope): use the shape transforms or effects, not node-level edits
editing many segments the same way: use Segments.All / Range and IVGSegmentRange.SetType or AddNode
cards.how: Bezier segment object of the VGCore model. A script reaches it from a curve shape: ActiveShape.Curve.Segments(i) (all subpaths), Curve.SubPaths(n).Segments(i) (one subpath), Segments.First / Last, from a node (IVGNode.Segment / NextSegment / PrevSegment) or by walking with Next / Previous. Offsets in the *At methods are read according to an OffsetType of the cdrSegmentOffsetType enum (default 2). Measurements come back in the document's unit.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: line or curve (cdrSegmentType); set it to turn a straight piece into a curve or the reverse

key_members.name: Length
key_members.use: length of this piece in document units

key_members.name: Index
key_members.use: position within its subpath (base 1)

key_members.name: AbsoluteIndex
key_members.use: position within the whole curve; use it with Curve.Segments(i)

key_members.name: StartNode
key_members.use: node where the segment begins

key_members.name: EndNode
key_members.use: node where the segment ends

key_members.name: StartingControlPointLength
key_members.use: length of the handle leaving the start node (curve segments)

key_members.name: StartingControlPointAngle
key_members.use: direction of the handle leaving the start node

key_members.name: EndingControlPointLength
key_members.use: length of the handle arriving at the end node

key_members.name: EndingControlPointAngle
key_members.use: direction of the handle arriving at the end node

key_members.name: SetStartingControlPointPosition
key_members.use: place the start handle at an exact x, y

key_members.name: SetEndingControlPointPosition
key_members.use: place the end handle at an exact x, y

key_members.name: GetPointAt
key_members.use: point on the segment at an offset, returned as an object (easiest from outside VBA)

key_members.name: GetPointPositionAt
key_members.use: x, y of a point at an offset, returned through ByRef arguments

key_members.name: GetTangentAt
key_members.use: tangent angle at an offset: rotate an object to follow the path

key_members.name: GetPerpendicularAt
key_members.use: perpendicular angle at an offset: ticks or labels standing off the path

key_members.name: AddNodeAt
key_members.use: insert a node at an offset and get it back

key_members.name: BreakApartAt
key_members.use: cut the path open at an offset

key_members.name: GetIntersections
key_members.use: crossing points with another segment

key_members.name: GetCopy
key_members.use: this piece as a separate curve, e.g. to draw it as its own object

gotchas: The default OffsetType 2 is the Bezier parameter (cdrParamSegmentOffset), so Offset 0.5 is not the midpoint by length on a curved segment; pass cdrRelativeSegmentOffset for a fraction of the length or cdrAbsoluteSegmentOffset for a distance from the start node (the enum says inches or the current document unit).

Lengths and positions are in ActiveDocument.Unit, which in a script is not necessarily the ruler unit; set ActiveDocument.Unit (e.g. cdrMillimeter) before reading or writing numbers (unverified that the default is inches in 25.1).

AddNodeAt and BreakApartAt change the curve: segment counts and indexes after the edit shift, so loop from the last segment backwards or re-read Curve.Segments (unverified that old Segment references go stale).
Only curve shapes have an editable Curve; rectangles, ellipses and text need ConvertToCurves first, and Shape.DisplayCurve returns a read-only curve (IVGShape batch), so use it for measuring only.
A line segment has no handles: set Type to cdrCurveSegment before writing the control-point members (unverified what writing them on a line segment does).

GetPointPositionAt, GetBoundingBox and the Get*ControlPointPosition methods return through ByRef arguments; from Python / pywin32 those come back as a returned tuple instead, so GetPointAt and BoundingBox are simpler there (unverified).
GetPeaks, GetBendPoints and FindParamOffset are described only as 'Gets Peaks' / 'Gets bend points' / 'Finds Parametric Offset'; test their outputs before building on them.
cards.example:
Dim seg As Segment, ang As Double
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrMillimeter
Set seg = ActiveShape.Curve.Segments(1)
Debug.Print seg.Type, seg.Length
ang = seg.GetTangentAt(0.5, cdrRelativeSegmentOffset)
seg.AddNodeAt 0.5, cdrRelativeSegmentOffset

review.changes: Absolute-offset gotcha now states the unit the cdrSegmentOffsetType enum gives. DisplayCurve gotcha changed from an unverified "copy" claim to the harvested "read-only curve" wording.

cards.name: IVGSegmentRange
cards.summary: A script-built list of segments from one curve, used to read or change several segments at once: their total length, whether they share a type, converting them all to lines or curves (SetType), adding a node at the middle of each (AddNode), getting their nodes as a node range, or selecting their controlling nodes. Adding to or removing from the range only changes the list, not the curve.
use_for: turning every straight segment of a traced logo or icon into curves in one call before smoothing
doubling node density on a path (a node in the middle of each segment) before applying a roughen or distortion
measuring the total length of part of a path, e.g. one side of a dieline
handing the nodes of chosen segments to a node-range operation via NodeRange
avoid: operations on one segment (handles, offsets, intersections): use IVGSegment
shape-level edits across several objects: use a ShapeRange instead
cards.how: Range (list) object over the segments of one curve. A script gets one from a segment collection: Curve.Segments.All, Segments.Range(Array(1, 3)) or Segments.AllExcluding(Array(...)) (SubPath.Segments works the same way), then grows or trims it with Add / AddRange / Remove / RemoveRange and works on it with SetType, AddNode, NodeRange or the selection methods. Item(i) is base 1 and For Each works through _NewEnum.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of segments in the range

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: segment i of the range (base 1, default member)

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: shared segment type, or cdrMixedSegments (2) when lines and curves are both present

key_members.name: Length
key_members.use: total length of the segments, in document units

key_members.name: SetType
key_members.use: make every segment in the range a line or a curve

key_members.name: AddNode
key_members.use: insert a node at the middle of each segment

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: append one segment to the list

key_members.name: AddRange
key_members.use: append all segments of another range

key_members.name: Remove
key_members.use: drop the i-th entry of the list (not from the curve)

key_members.name: RemoveRange
key_members.use: drop the segments of another range from this list

key_members.name: RemoveAll
key_members.use: empty the list

key_members.name: NodeRange
key_members.use: the nodes that belong to these segments, as a node range

key_members.name: FirstSegment
key_members.use: first segment in the range

key_members.name: LastSegment
key_members.use: last segment in the range

key_members.name: CreateSelection
key_members.use: select the nodes that control these segments

key_members.name: AddToSelection
key_members.use: add those nodes to the current node selection

key_members.name: RemoveFromSelection
key_members.use: take those nodes out of the node selection

gotchas: Add, AddRange, Remove, RemoveRange and RemoveAll edit only the list; nothing is deleted from the curve. Only SetType and AddNode (and the selection calls) change the document.
Remove(Index) uses the position inside the range (base 1), not the segment's Index or AbsoluteIndex in the curve.
Type is read-only on the range and reports cdrMixedSegments (2) when lines and curves are both present; use SetType to write.
After AddNode the curve has more segments than the range lists; rebuild the range from Curve.Segments before a second pass (unverified).
Mixing segments from different curves in one range is probably refused or ignored, since Parent is a single curve (unverified).
CreateSelection selects nodes, which a user only sees while the Shape tool is active (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim sr As SegmentRange
ActiveDocument.Unit = cdrMillimeter
Set sr = ActiveShape.Curve.Segments.All
Debug.Print sr.Count, sr.Length, sr.Type
sr.SetType cdrCurveSegment
sr.AddNode

review.changes: Named the mixed value of Type as cdrMixedSegments (2), from the cdr_api_x03 cdrSegmentType enum. Otherwise no change.

cards.name: IVGSegments
cards.summary: The read-only collection of all segments of a curve (Curve.Segments) or of one subpath (SubPath.Segments). It lets a script count and walk the pieces of a path and build segment ranges from all, some, or all-but-some of them; it does not add or delete segments itself.
use_for: looping over every segment of a path to measure, decorate or adjust it
picking the first / last piece of an open path, e.g. to add arrowhead-style ornaments at the ends
building a segment range of selected pieces (Range / AllExcluding) for a batch SetType or AddNode
avoid: adding segments: append them through the subpath (AppendLineSegment / AppendCurveSegment on IVGSubPath) or draw a new curve
node-level work (cusp / smooth / symmetric nodes): use Curve.Nodes and IVGNode
cards.how: Collection object returned by IVGCurve.Segments (every segment in every subpath, in order) and IVGSubPath.Segments (that subpath only), e.g. ActiveShape.Curve.Segments. Item(i) is base 1 and is the default member, so Segments(i) works; For Each works through _NewEnum. Range, All and AllExcluding return an IVGSegmentRange.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of segments

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: segment i (base 1, default member)

key_members.name: First
key_members.use: first segment

key_members.name: Last
key_members.use: last segment

key_members.name: All
key_members.use: segment range holding every segment

key_members.name: Range
key_members.use: segment range from an array of indexes

key_members.name: AllExcluding
key_members.use: segment range of every segment except the listed indexes

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: enables For Each over the collection

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the curve the collection belongs to

gotchas: Curve.Segments spans all subpaths while SubPath.Segments covers one; Segment.Index counts within the subpath and Segment.AbsoluteIndex within the curve, so index Curve.Segments with AbsoluteIndex.
Parent is typed as a curve although its description says 'parent subpath'; do not expect an IVGSubPath back.
Range and AllExcluding take an array of indexes (VBA Array(1, 3)); a bare number is not an array (unverified how pywin32 lists marshal here).
The collection follows the live curve: after AddNodeAt / BreakApartAt / AddNode the Count and the meaning of each index change (unverified).
A closed subpath has as many segments as nodes, an open one has one fewer; do not mix Nodes and Segments indexes (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim segs As Segments, s As Segment
Set segs = ActiveShape.Curve.Segments
For Each s In segs
  Debug.Print s.AbsoluteIndex, s.Type, s.Length
Next s
segs.AllExcluding(Array(1, segs.Count)).SetType cdrCurveSegment

cards.name: IVGSelectionInformation
cards.summary: Read-only report on the document's current selection: how many objects are selected, what kind they are (group, text, bitmap, blend / contour / extrude / drop shadow / distortion / envelope / fitted text / connector and their control objects), what can be done with them (blend, contour, clone, ungroup, copy an effect, apply fill / outline / transparency, lock) and the editing state (text editing, inside PowerClip contents). It also hands back the parts of a compound effect, such as a blend's top and bottom shapes or a drop shadow's control shape.
use_for: guarding a macro: exit cleanly when nothing is selected, text is being edited or the selection is the wrong kind
reaching the source object behind an effect, e.g. recolouring the control shape of a drop shadow or contour, or the ends of a blend
routing a batch tool by selection type: artistic vs paragraph text, bitmaps, groups, linked bitmaps
checking CanCreateBlend / CanApplyContour / CanApplyTransparency before calling the effect so the script does not throw
avoid: getting the selected shapes themselves for editing: use ActiveSelectionRange or ActiveDocument.SelectionRange (ActiveDocument.Selection returns one cdrSelectionShape shape, not a range)
scripts that never select anything (working on ShapeRanges directly): this object only describes the user-visible selection
cards.how: Selection-state helper of the VGCore model, reached as ActiveDocument.SelectionInfo (an IVGDocument member); Parent is the document. Every member is a read-only bool, count, type or shape reference describing the selection at the time it is read; nothing on it changes the document.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of selected objects; 0 means nothing selected

key_members.name: FirstShape
key_members.use: first selected shape

key_members.name: SecondShape
key_members.use: second selected shape, for two-object operations such as blends

key_members.name: IsEditingText
key_members.use: True while the user is typing in a text object: skip shape edits

key_members.name: IsOnPowerClipContents
key_members.use: True while inside PowerClip contents editing

key_members.name: IsGroup
key_members.use: the selected shape is a group

key_members.name: CanUngroup
key_members.use: some selected shape can be ungrouped

key_members.name: CanCreateBlend
key_members.use: the selected shapes can be blended

key_members.name: IsBlendGroup
key_members.use: the selected shape is a blend group

key_members.name: BlendTopShape
key_members.use: top end shape of the selected blend

key_members.name: BlendBottomShape
key_members.use: bottom end shape of the selected blend

key_members.name: BlendPath
key_members.use: path of a blend that follows a path

key_members.name: IsDropShadowGroup
key_members.use: the selected shape is a drop shadow group

key_members.name: DropShadowControlShape
key_members.use: the object that casts the selected drop shadow

key_members.name: IsContourGroup
key_members.use: the selected shape is a contour group

key_members.name: ContourControlShape
key_members.use: the object the selected contour is built from

key_members.name: ExtrudeFaceShape
key_members.use: the face object of the selected extrude

key_members.name: IsArtisticTextSelected
key_members.use: the selection is artistic text

key_members.name: IsParagraphTextSelected
key_members.use: the selection is paragraph text

key_members.name: IsBitmapSelected
key_members.use: some selected shape is a bitmap

gotchas: The VBA type is the coclass SelectionInfo (Dim si As SelectionInfo); there is no SelectionInformation type in the 25.1 type library, only the IVGSelectionInformation interface, so 'As SelectionInformation' does not compile (unverified in the VBA editor).

Several harvested descriptions are shifted by one line: IsConnector says 'is a fitted text', IsFittedText 'fitted text control', IsFittedTextControl 'natural media control', IsNaturalMediaControl 'natural media group' and IsNaturalMediaGroup 'an envelope'. Go by the member name and test on a real selection before relying on these (unverified which is right).
CanCloneDropShadow is described as 'blend can be copied' and IsMeshFillSelected / IsMeshFillPresent share one description; the same caution applies.

The plain Is* members (IsGroup, IsBlendGroup, IsDropShadowGroup ...) describe 'the selected shape'; most *Selected / *Present members (IsBitmapSelected, IsGroupSelected, IsEnvelopePresent ...) describe 'any of the selected shapes'. IsArtisticTextSelected, IsParagraphTextSelected, IsTextSelected and IsOLESelected are exceptions: they are described as 'the selected shape' too. Use the 'any of' members for multi-object selections.
The control / group getters (BlendTopShape, DropShadowControlShape, ContourGroup ...) are only meaningful when the matching Is* member is True; otherwise expect Nothing (unverified).

It describes the user-visible selection only: a macro that works on ShapeRanges without selecting must call CreateSelection first, and reading it while Application.Optimization is True may see a stale state (unverified).
What decides FirstShape vs SecondShape (selection order or stacking order) is not documented (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim si As SelectionInfo
Set si = ActiveDocument.SelectionInfo
If si.Count = 0 Or si.IsEditingText Then Exit Sub
Debug.Print si.Count, si.IsGroup, si.CanUngroup
If si.IsBlendGroup Then Debug.Print si.BlendTopShape.Type, si.BlendBottomShape.Type
If si.CanCreateBlend Then si.FirstShape.CreateBlend si.SecondShape

review.changes: Example declared 'As SelectionInformation', a type the type library does not have; changed to the coclass SelectionInfo (cdr_api_23) and added a gotcha. Fixed the *Selected gotcha: IsArtisticTextSelected, IsParagraphTextSelected, IsTextSelected and IsOLESelected describe 'the selected shape', not 'any of'. avoid now points to ActiveDocument.SelectionRange, because Document.Selection returns a single selection shape.
